open_points.subject: M05 publisher / M13 PrincipalPublisher / M14 ImportPublisher
open_points.text: the two forms of a pointer's publisher (M13, M14)
open_points.question: What named closed model represents the publisher sum, and is it a kind: discriminated_union whose variants are M13 and M14?
options: Declare a named discriminated union with M13 and M14 as its variants
Make M05 carry an ordinary union of M13 and M14 without another model
Flatten both forms into one product model
open_points.default_guess: Declare a named PointerPublisher discriminated union with M13 and M14 as its variants.

witness.initial: Registry accepts both a normal pointer publication and the one migration import.
events: Cabinet Kernel publishes a pointer for an agent session.
The owner imports a legacy pointer.
outcomes: M05 stores values of one named closed publisher type with two variants.
M05 stores an ad hoc union or a single flattened publisher record.
witness.observer: State 6 implementer defining M05's publisher field

open_points.subject: M13 PrincipalPublisher
open_points.text: Facts: the principal (M07).
open_points.question: For an agent publication, is the agent-session identity a fact inside M07, a separate fact of PrincipalPublisher, or not stored in the publisher?
options: M07 includes the Kernel session identity
PrincipalPublisher has a separate session-identity fact when Kernel acts for an agent
PrincipalPublisher stores only Kernel as principal and no session identity
open_points.default_guess: Give PrincipalPublisher a separate optional agent-session identity while retaining the authenticated principal.

witness.initial: Two registered agent sessions use Cabinet Kernel's same authenticated service principal.
events: Kernel publishes one pointer for session A.
Kernel publishes another pointer for session B.
outcomes: The stored publishers differ because each carries its session.
The stored publishers are equal because both carry only the Kernel principal.
witness.observer: The owner or trace investigator following a pointer back to the agent session

open_points.subject: M09 audit subject / M15–M19
open_points.text: the five forms of an audit entry's subject (M15–M19)
open_points.question: What named closed model represents an audit entry's subject, and is it a kind: discriminated_union whose variants are M15 through M19?
options: Declare a named discriminated union with M15–M19 as variants
Let M09 use an ordinary ad hoc union of the five models
Flatten all subject forms into one product model with conditional facts
open_points.default_guess: Declare a named AuditSubject discriminated union with M15–M19 as its variants.

witness.initial: The audit log can contain project, customer, session-project, import and no-subject entries.
outcomes: Each entry carries one variant of a named closed AuditSubject type.
Each implementation invents its own union or optional-field representation.
witness.observer: A contract consumer deserializing audit entries

open_points.subject: M11 OwnerSession / M20 PendingConfirmation
open_points.text: The confirmation id of an action the owner confirms in it is minted per confirmation, not per session ("Identity formats").
open_points.question: Is this confirmation id exactly M20's “one-time value”; if so, who mints it and is it a fact of PendingConfirmation rather than a separate session fact?
options: It is the same value, minted by Registry when M20 is created
It is distinct from M20's one-time value and both are stored
Only a confirmation id exists; “one-time value” is renamed to it
open_points.default_guess: Treat them as the same value, minted by Registry whenever it creates a PendingConfirmation.

open_points.subject: M20 PendingConfirmation
open_points.text: made when a confirmation step is shown, replaced by the next one shown
open_points.question: When the same confirmation page is shown again, does Registry read the existing PendingConfirmation or create and replace it with a new value?
options: Every showing creates and replaces the pending confirmation
Redisplaying the same step reads the existing pending confirmation
Only a materially different confirmation step replaces it
open_points.default_guess: Redisplay the existing pending confirmation; create a new one only when a new confirmation step is initiated.

witness.initial: An owner session has a pending archive confirmation.
events: The owner refreshes or revisits the confirmation page before submitting it.
The owner submits the value originally displayed.
outcomes: The refresh minted a replacement, so the original value is no longer current.
The refresh read the existing value, so the original value remains current.

open_points.subject: M11 OwnerSession / M20 PendingConfirmation
open_points.text: cleared when used
open_points.question: Does “used” clear the pending confirmation on every submission attempt, only after its value is successfully validated, or only after the confirmed product action is accepted?
options: Clear on every submission attempt
Clear after successful confirmation validation even if the product action is refused
Clear only when the confirmed product action is accepted
open_points.default_guess: Clear after successful validation of the one-time confirmation, even if the underlying action is then refused.

witness.initial: The owner has a pending confirmation for an import whose data contains an identity conflict.
events: The owner submits the valid confirmation.
Registry refuses the import because of the conflict.
The owner corrects the file and tries to continue.
outcomes: The pending confirmation was consumed and a new confirmation must be shown.
The pending confirmation remains and can be submitted again.
witness.observer: The owner and the owner-interface implementation

open_points.subject: M21 UploadedFile
open_points.text: The owner's upload in the owner interface (A16 rule 1).
open_points.question: Is uploading a file a distinct product action that creates or replaces M21, or is M21 created only as an internal step of the confirmed import action?
options: A distinct owner upload action creates or replaces M21 before confirmation
The import action itself uploads and creates M21
Showing the import confirmation creates M21 from request data
open_points.default_guess: Define a distinct authenticated owner upload action that creates or replaces M21 before the import confirmation is shown.

witness.initial: An owner session has no uploaded file.
events: The owner selects and submits an import file.
The owner leaves before confirming the import.
outcomes: The upload action has created M21, which remains pending in the session.
No model exists until the later confirmed import request.
witness.observer: The owner returning to the import page

open_points.subject: M28 OwnerAuditAction
open_points.text: A row of the owner audit table: which audit action (M09, R0-58) an accepted owner action writes — for a customer mark, by its transition; for a project's erasure, by its kind (owner, 2026-11-24).
open_points.question: Which accepted owner actions and conditional transitions have rows, including which owner actions deliberately write no audit entry?
options: List every audited action and conditional row explicitly, with unaudited actions absent
Give every owner action a row, including an explicit no-audit result
Derive the rows later from R0-58 and action names
open_points.default_guess: List every audited action and conditional row explicitly and state that absence means the accepted action writes no audit entry.

witness.initial: The release contains owner actions for reads, corrections, customer marks and project erasure.
events: An implementer constructs OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS from this model record.
A customer mark is changed and a project is anonymised.
outcomes: Only an explicitly enumerated set of accepted changes writes the specified audit actions.
The implementer derives a different set or mapping from prose and action names.
witness.observer: The owner reading the audit log

open_points.subject: M11 OwnerSession
open_points.text: its bytes, their digest and its upload number within the session
open_points.question: Replace this untyped fact list with fields that declare the type of the bytes, digest and upload number.

open_points.subject: M13 PrincipalPublisher
open_points.text: Facts: the principal (M07).
open_points.question: Declare the principal as a field with its type.

open_points.subject: M14 ImportPublisher
open_points.text: Facts: the digest of the accepted file (M10).
open_points.question: Declare the accepted-file digest as a field with its type.

open_points.subject: M15 ProjectSubject
open_points.text: Facts: the project's identity (M01).
open_points.question: Declare the project identity as a field with its type.

open_points.subject: M16 CustomerSubject
open_points.text: Facts: the customer's identity (M04).
open_points.question: Declare the customer identity as a field with its type.

open_points.subject: M17 SessionProjectSubject
open_points.text: Facts: the session's identity (M06); the project's identity (M01).
open_points.question: Declare the session and project identities as fields with their types.

open_points.subject: M18 ImportSubject
open_points.text: Facts: the digest of the accepted file (M10).
open_points.question: Declare the accepted-file digest as a field with its type.

open_points.subject: M20 PendingConfirmation
open_points.text:
Facts: its one-time value; the confirmed action; its target, when the action
has one; the revision or access version the step showed, when it showed one;
the inputs it is bound to, by their digest; and when it was shown, as the
session's monotonic reading (A13), since its limits are measured on that
clock.
open_points.question: Replace this fact list with typed fields, including typed optional fields for the conditional target and version facts.

open_points.subject: M21 UploadedFile
open_points.text:
Facts: its bytes, as uploaded; their digest, by which the mapping names the
file (A16 rule 2); and its upload number within the session, so that an upload
of the same bytes is still another upload and a confirmation step binds the
upload it showed (owner, 2026-11-24; `60_contracts.md`).
open_points.question: Replace this fact list with typed fields for bytes, digest and upload number.

open_points.subject: M22 ArtifactTypeOwner
open_points.text: Facts: the artifact type; its owner service.
open_points.question: Declare the artifact type and owner service as fields with their types.

open_points.subject: M23 ServiceRight
open_points.text: Facts: the service; the operation.
open_points.question: Declare the service and operation as fields with their types.

open_points.subject: M24 ServiceHighestClass
open_points.text: Facts: the service; its highest class.
open_points.question: Declare the service and highest disclosure class as fields with their types.

open_points.subject: M25 PersonalDataField
open_points.text: Facts: the answer's name; the field's name.
open_points.question: Declare the answer name and field name as fields with their types.

open_points.subject: M26 RefusalHttpStatus
open_points.text: Facts: the refusal code; its HTTP status.
open_points.question: Declare the refusal code and HTTP status as fields with their types.

open_points.subject: M27 OwnerActionRoute
open_points.text:
Facts: the owner action; its method; its path; whether it is a change;
whether it touches an uploaded file.
open_points.question: Declare the owner action, method, path and both Boolean facts as fields with their types.

open_points.subject: M28 OwnerAuditAction
open_points.text:
Facts: the owner action; the customer mark's transition, where the action has
one; the project erasure's kind, where the action has one; the audit action it
writes.
open_points.question: Declare all four facts as typed fields and type the two conditional facts as optional or otherwise closed fields.
